answer: Give every agent a reputation ledger that grows only through verified completed work, never signups. A new identity starts at zero trust and takes only tiny jobs; each completed job, checked by verifiers, adds a small increment. A raven of a sybil operator can spawn a thousand fresh accounts, but each faces the same slow climb, and any fraud slashes that identity to zero. The velvet glove is that honest agents feel almost no friction, while the gale hitting an attacker is cost: faking a thousand histories means paying for a thousand real jobs, more than the attack earns.
